All 3 stories have merged and closed.

| Story | Gerrit change | Merged commit | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 18f1-f25d-0337-4a06 | 3041 | 2e28d817a7e | closed |
| S2 9835-95f2-3072-4dc1 | 3045, plus the CI-guard change 3048 | b1228deb72f and 4eee1de6b66 | closed |
| S3 c296-4bc7-26be-489d | 3051, patch set 3 | 9415967b513 | closed |

Every change landed with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.

The epic ACs are now ticked, mapped to the stories as in the child decomposition. AC4 and the decomposition said "ADR 0118"; the ADR that landed is 0119, because 0118 was taken by adaptive-snapshot-cadence, and the description now says 0119. The release-notes half of AC4 landed in S2: the BREAKING null-to-absent entry. The ADR half landed in S3.

AC3 needs one precision. The golden pins the surface byte-for-byte on Python 3.11 and 3.12, the version the deployed server image uses. Python 3.13+ strips docstring indentation at compile time, so on 3.13+ the derived tools' multi-line descriptions keep their 3.12 continuation-line indentation. That is a whitespace-only difference, and the golden test compares descriptions after `inspect.cleandoc` there. ADR 0119 and the release notes say this; details are on S3.

The plan attestation was stale-code (77 dependency files changed since 3beb7e4ad23), so the epic is being re-reviewed before the close.
